title: WPSS/1469/2018 of MANISH KUMAR KANDPAL Vs GOVERNMENT OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH ITS SECRETARY

JUDGMENT: (per the Acting Chief Justice Shri Manoj Kumar Tiwari)
Since common question of law and facts are
involved in these petitions, therefore, they are being
heard and decided together. However for the sake of
brevity, facts of Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1552 of 2018
alone are being considered and discussed.
2. The reliefs sought in the Writ Petition (S/S)
No.1552 of 2018 are as follows:
"(i) Issue a writ, rule, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari for quashing the impugned
order dated 24.05.2018 (Annexure no.7) whereby

3
the candidate of the petitioner for appointment on
the post of X-Ray Technician was rejected by the
respondent no.2.
(i)(a):- To issue a writ or order to declare sub
rule (3) of Rule 8 of Uttarakhand X-Ray
Technician Service Rules, 2015 as ultra vires
to the extent of registration of a candidate
with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council.
(i)(b):- To issue a writ or order in the nature
of Certiorari quashing condition 2 of
Educational qualification for post code- 11, X-Ray Technician of advertisement dated
20.02.2016 to the extent of registration of a
candidate with Uttarakhand Para Medical
Council in Uttarakhand Medical Health and
Family Welfare Department.
(ii) Issue a writ, rule, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding and directing
the respondent no.2 to send the name of the
petitioner for appointment on the post of X-Ray
Technician to the respondent no.3."
3. Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection
Commission (respondent no.2) issued an
advertisement on 20.02.2016 inviting applications,
inter alia, for the post of X-Ray Technician. One of
the condition of eligibility for the post of X-Ray
Technician, as mentioned in the advertisement, was
that one should possess Registration Certificate from
Uttarakhand State Medical Faculty or Uttarakhand
Para Medical Council. Rule 8(3) of Uttarakhand X-Ray
Technician Service Rules, 2015 also contain similar
provision regarding Registration Certificate.
4. Petitioners responded to the aforesaid
advertisement and they were permitted to participate
in the selection process. After declaration of result,

4
when the documents of successful candidates were
being verified, it was found by the Selecting Body
that petitioners were not registered with Uttarakhand
Para Medical Council upto the last date of submission
of online application, consequently, their candidature
was rejected. Thus, feeling aggrieved, petitioners
have approached this Court challenging the order
passed by Selecting Body, rejecting their candidature.
Petitioners have also challenged validity of Rule 8(3)
of the applicable Recruitment Rules. They have also
challenged the condition regarding registration with
Uttarakhand Para Medical Council, as mentioned in
the advertisement.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material available on record. Learned
counsel for the petitioner contended that since
petitioner is educationally qualified for appointment
as X-Ray Technician, as he possess Diploma in X-Ray
Technician Course from a recognized institute,
therefore, he cannot be non-suited for appointment
only because there was some delay on the part of
Uttarakhand Para Medical Council in issuing
Registration Certificate. He further argued that the
advertisement is silent as to the date upto which
Registration Certificate has to be possessed by a
candidate.
6. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for
the Selecting Body would submit that registration
with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council is an essential

5
condition as per the applicable Rules and also the
advertisement, therefore, anyone who is not
registered with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council on
or before the last date of submission of application,
cannot be treated as eligible. He further submits that
petitioners took a chance by submitting application
despite stipulation in the advertisement that anyone
not registered with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council
will not be treated as eligible and there would be
many others who despite having Diploma in relevant
subject, would not have applied due to the condition
mentioned in the advertisement regarding
registration. Thus, he submits that any relaxation
given to petitioners would cause injustice to those
who refrained from applying due to the condition
regarding registration with Uttarakhand Para Medical
Council. He further submitted that it is settled
position that one must possess all conditions of
eligibility on or before last date of submission of
application for appointment to a post and since
petitioners did not possess one of the essential
condition of eligibility upto the last date of submission
of application, therefore, petitioners are not entitled
to any relief.
7. Rule 8 of the applicable Recruitment Rules
deal with academic qualification. The same is
extracted below:

8. From perusal of Rule 8, it is revealed that,
for appointment as X-Ray Technician, one should
fulfill 4 conditions:
(a) He should have passed intermediate
examination from Secondary Education Board
Uttarakhand with Science subjects or any other
examination declared by the State Government as
equivalent thereto.
(b) He should possess Diploma or Degree in X-Ray
Technician/Technology, which is registrable with
Uttarakhand State Medical Faculty or Uttarakhand
Para Medical Council.
(c) He should have Certificate of Registration with
Uttarakhand State Medical Faculty or Uttarakhand
Para Medical Council besides registration with an
employment office within the State of Uttarakhand.
(d) Workable knowledge of Hindi.
9. Candidature of the petitioners has been
rejected on the ground that they were not registered
with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council upto the last
date of submission of application, which is referable
to Rule 8(3) of the applicable service Rules.
10. Learned counsel for the petitioner

7
contended that since the Diploma possessed by
petitioner is registrable with Uttarakhand Para
Medical Council in terms of Rule 8(2), therefore, their
candidature could not be rejected only on the ground
that they were not having Registration Certificate
upto the last date of submission of application. Thus,
according to them, Rule 8(2) and Rule 8(3) of the
service Rules have to be read harmoniously and
anyone who possess Degree/Diploma, which is
registrable with State Medical Faculty/ Uttarakhand
Para Medical Council should be treated as eligible for
appointment as X-Ray Technician. The said
submission made on behalf of petitioners is bereft of
merit. The State Government, as employer, is
entitled to prescribe conditions of eligibility for the
post of X-Ray Technician. The State Government has
prescribed registration with Uttarakhand Para Medical
Council as one of the essential condition of eligibility,
therefore, the Selecting Body cannot overlook or
relax the condition prescribed by the State
Government in the Statutory Rules. Although, Rule
8(2) talks about a Degree or Diploma, which is
registrable with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council/
State Medical Faculty, however, Rule 8(3) goes one
step further and provides that, without registration
with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council/State Medical
Faculty, one shall not be eligible for appointment.
Thus, the submission that Rule 8(2) and Rule 8(3)
should be read harmoniously and the condition of
registration with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council

8
should be dispensed with, cannot be accepted. Both
Rule 8(2) and Rule 8(3) provide for independent
conditions of eligibility and anyone, who does not
meet the requirement of Rule 8(2) and Rule 8(3),
cannot be treated as eligible.
11. Petitioners have challenged validity of Rule
8(3), however, the ground taken for challenging
validity of the Rules is not sufficient for holding the
Rules unconstitutional. Validity of Rules which are
statutory, can be challenged only on the ground that
they violate the provision contained in Part III of the
Constitution or on the ground of lack of legislative
competence. None of these grounds are made out by
the petitioners.
12. There is another aspect of the matter. X-Ray Technician is a professional course and the State
Legislature has enacted Uttarakhand Para Medical
Council Act, 2009, under which a regulatory body
known as 'Uttarakhand Para Medical Council' has
been established. As per the scheme of the Act, one
needs to be registered with Uttarakhand Para Medical
Council for practicing as X-Ray Technician, within the
State. Thus, the State, as employer, cannot appoint a
person as X-Ray Technician who is not registered
with Uttarakhand Para Medical Council.
13. Even otherwise also, there is no disharmony
between Rule 8(2) and Rule 8(3) of the applicable
Recruitment Rules, which may necessitate reading

9
down of Rule 8(3), as submitted on behalf of
petitioner.
14. The fact of the matter is that petitioners
were not eligible for the post of X-Ray Technician
even as per the condition mentioned in the
advertisement. They submitted application pursuant
to the advertisement in question and when they were
declared ineligible, they have approached this Court
challenging the advertisement and the Rules.
Whether challenge thrown by the petitioners to the
advertisement / Rules, after participating in the
selection, can be entertained, is yet another aspect
on which the writ petition would fail. Thus, in our
considered opinion, any interference in the matter
would not be warranted.
15. Accordingly, the writ petitions fail and are
dismissed. There will be no order as to costs.
 ___________________ MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, ACJ.

 VIVEK BHARTI SHARMA, J.
